glosses: Capable of developing past the egg stage.

glosses: Highly fertile; able to produce offspring.

examples.text: The number of children per woman depends, as has been said, on biological and social factors which determine: (1) the frequency of births during a woman's fecund period, and (2) the portion of the fecund period--between puberty and menopause--effectively utilized for reproduction.
The druids […] believed that mistletoe could make barren animals fecund, and that it was an antidote to all poisons.

glosses: Leading to new ideas or innovation.

examples.text: This idea of Aristotle's has proved marvellously fecund; and in truth it is the only idea covering quite the whole area of cenoscopy that has shown any marked uberosity.

examples.text: Die Fische in meinem Aquarium sind sehr fruchtbar.
Von Kaninchen sagt man, sie seien sehr fruchtbar.

glosses: so, dass es viele Früchte hervorbringt

examples.text: Carls Großvater kaufte sich vor 60 Jahren ein fruchtbares Stück Land, von dessen Erträgen nun die ganze Familie leben kann.
„Pro Sekunde gehen weltweit vier Fußballfelder fruchtbarer Boden verloren – durch Dürre, Erosion und Bodenversiegelung.“
„Dadurch bildeten sich breite, von fruchtbarem Schwemmland bedeckte Flussterrassen.“

glosses: mit Erfolg

examples.text: Ich freue mich auf eine fruchtbare Zusammenarbeit mit den neuen Kollegen.
„Eine Sinnkrise im Alltag oder Berufsleben kann für den dynamischen Menschen und Sinnsucher ein fruchtbarer Moment, ein Auslöser sein, auf Entdeckungsreise nach Alternativen zu gehen.“

glosses: способный приносить плоды
Fertile; producing offspring or fruit in abundance, applied to plants producing fruit, animals producing young, etc.
Similarly producing results or performing deeds in abundance.

examples.text: However appealing Antibes may be to migrant authors, indigenous ones are relatively scarce. A notable exception is Jacques Audiberti, Antibes-born novelist and prolific playwright who wrote in the turn-of-the-century surrealist style, with titles that translate as Slaughter, or In Favour of Infanticide.

The most obvious beneficiary of the visitors' superiority was Frank Lampard. By the end of the night he was perched 13th in the list of England's most prolific goalscorers, having leapfrogged Sir Geoff Hurst to score his 24th and 25th international goals. No other player has managed more than the Chelsea midfielder's 11 in World Cup qualification ties, with this a display to roll back the years.
A Chinese PhD student who is "one of the most prolific predators" in the UK has been sentenced to life with a minimum term of 24 years.
